evidence_trigger: 2025 eviction filings were 55.2 per 1,000 estimated renter households, above the City benchmark of 40.2; vulnerability was at the 73.9% percentile and transaction activity fell 33.2% between 2015-17 and 2022-24.
proposed_city_response: Prioritize eviction-prevention outreach, legal representation referral, and emergency rental-assistance navigation before a filing becomes a completed displacement.
monitoring_metric: Filings per 1,000 renter households; cases receiving legal or rental-assistance referral
claim_boundary: Filings are court cases, not unique households or completed evictions.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence

evidence_trigger: Median sale-price CAGR was 17.0%, the fastest in the qualifying set. Prices rose 285.5% from 2014 to 2024 versus income growth of 46.0%, a gap of 239.6 percentage points. Vulnerability was 73.9%.
proposed_city_response: Begin targeted preservation and acquisition screening for naturally occurring affordable rental properties; evaluate land-bank or community land-trust pathways where parcel-level due diligence supports action.
monitoring_metric: At-risk affordable units screened, preserved, or acquired; price and rent trajectory
claim_boundary: ZIP-level price growth does not identify a specific property at risk.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence

evidence_trigger: The ZIP has rapid price growth (17.0%) and an estimated homeowner share of 48.9%; the analysis does not yet contain parcel-level tax delinquency or assessment-growth data.
proposed_city_response: Pair outreach for LOOP, installment agreements, tangled-title support, and housing counseling with a future delinquency/assessment eligibility screen before targeting individual owners.
monitoring_metric: Eligible owners contacted and enrolled; delinquency and assessment-growth indicators
claim_boundary: This is a prevention pathway, not evidence that tax pressure caused current sales patterns.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence

evidence_trigger: 191 dwelling units were reported on 2023-2025 new-construction permits (72.2% percentile; 13.2 per 1,000 occupied units); reported units are a pipeline measure, not completed supply.
proposed_city_response: Track permit issuance, completion, affordability commitments, investor ownership, inventory, and days on market together before interpreting development as either relief or added displacement pressure.
monitoring_metric: Permitted versus completed units; affordable-unit commitments; inventory and days on market
claim_boundary: Permit records do not prove construction, completion, net supply, or affordability.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence

evidence_trigger: The 2024 price-to-income ratio was 3.94x and prices rose 184.3% from 2014 to 2024 versus income growth of 42.3%, a gap of 142 percentage points. Renter share was 53.3% and renter cost burden 64.4%.
proposed_city_response: Prioritize preservation screening for renter-occupied properties and connect expiring or unsubsidized affordable stock to acquisition, repair, or affordability-preservation resources.
monitoring_metric: Renter-occupied units screened and preserved; price-to-income and rent-burden trajectory
claim_boundary: Median changes can reflect household composition as well as within-household change.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence

evidence_trigger: 201 dwelling units were reported on 2023-2025 new-construction permits, slightly above 19132's 191. 19132 has the higher pipeline percentile (72.2% vs 61.1%) and rate per 1,000 occupied units (13.2 vs 7); 19143's High priority reflects its 3.94x price-to-income ratio and 53.3% renter share.
proposed_city_response: Track whether permitted projects start, complete, and include affordable units; connect high-impact projects to preservation and community-benefit review where existing City authority applies.
monitoring_metric: Units permitted, started, completed, and affordability-restricted
claim_boundary: Reported permit units are proposed pipeline, not delivered or affordable units.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence

evidence_trigger: The 2025 filing rate was 34.7 per 1,000 estimated renter households, below the City benchmark of 40.2 and the 38.9% percentile. Renter share was 53.3% and renter cost burden 64.4%.
proposed_city_response: Maintain targeted legal-aid and rental-assistance outreach, but do not describe 19143 as the higher filing-rate case; use building- or tract-level hotspots if operational targeting is required.
delivery_lead_time: Immediate monitoring; targeted outreach as triggered
monitoring_metric: Filing rate, renter burden, and service uptake
claim_boundary: A below-city filing rate does not mean that no renter households are at risk.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence

evidence_trigger: The 2024 price-to-income ratio was 3.94x and transaction activity fell 13.9% between 2015-17 and 2022-24, a milder contraction than 19132. The dashboard lacks mortgage origination and denial data, so buyer-side barriers cannot be assigned yet.
proposed_city_response: Monitor mortgage access, first-time-buyer participation, inventory, and days on market before proposing buyer-side assistance; test whether the barrier is price, credit, supply, or another mechanism.
monitoring_metric: Originations by borrower and property type; inventory; days on market; denial reasons
claim_boundary: Current RTT and Redfin data do not identify mortgage applicants or denial causes.
evidence_standard: Conditionally supported by current descriptive evidence
